fixture_history.change: initial: only-name, declared-elsewhere, extension-carrier, map, zone, mapless pin, legacy map, and the id-less skip

ADDITIVE: the empty-string name and the explicit-nulls element joined elements[], and not-json.json joined skipped_files[], during the S334 session on 2026-07-28. They shipped under the UNCHANGED string 1.0.0 for three days, so 'fixture v1.0.0' named two different artifacts and any pass reported against it is ambiguous. Versioned retroactively here: a reader that found 8 ran 1.1.0. Same defect class as the stale prose count below, one layer down — the field that exists to make divergence honest was itself not maintained.

ADDITIVE: on-the-map, a pin whose map link uses the format's BARE spelling (`map`, not atlas's `map_id`). The first folder another tool wrote with pins on it opened in atlas with every pin missing and the map index reading 0: atlas keyed on its own suffixed name and never looked under the spec's. A reader must resolve the link under the spec spelling; a writer must not rewrite the key as a side effect of opening the folder.

elements.name: Only Name
elements.note: type is ABSENT in the body; a reader may infer it from the directory or serve it untyped, but must not invent timestamps. RECOMMENDED READING (Quillon, Armature, adopted 2026-07-29): infer from the directory but FLAG the inference rather than presenting it as a declaration, and never write it back. See README 'Where two readings are permitted'

elements.name: Declared Elsewhere
elements.note: sits in elements/character/ and declares location — the body wins

elements.name: Extension Carrier
elements.note: x_probe_note must survive a read-write round trip unchanged

elements.name: Wandering Pin
elements.note: MAPLESS by design — no map, no element. Must not crash, must not be given one
name is the EMPTY STRING, which is legal. Not the same as absent, and must not be replaced with a placeholder on disk. A reader may display a fallback; it must not write one back

elements.name: Null Fields
elements.note: explicit nulls on single links, multi links, a date and a text field. null means UNSET and is never the same claim as 0 or empty-string; a reader must not collapse it

elements.name: On the Map
elements.note: links its map under the SPEC spelling `map` (bare link names, §5), never `map_id`. A reader must resolve it to The Territory. A writer that touches this file for any other reason must keep the key as `map`; a reader must not migrate it

legacy_elements.name: Legacy Map
legacy_elements.note: lives in spatial/map/ — NOT normative. A reader that covers only elements/ is conforming and reports 8; a legacy-tolerant reader (atlas) reports 9. CORRECTED 2026-07-29. The note said 6 and 7, and it was RIGHT when written: the committed fixture held 6 elements. S334 added two more (the empty-string name and the explicit nulls) and did not update the prose beneath them, so a hand-written count rotted the moment the machine-readable list grew. Caught by Quillon's independent reader, whose count matched elements[] id-for-id. Derive counts from the array or expect them to lie.

skipped_files.reason: truncated mid-key — unparseable. A reader must skip it, keep serving every other element, and NOT delete it. One malformed file must never take out the world

reader_report_shape.found: count of elements[] your reader loaded
reader_report_shape.found_legacy: count of legacy_elements[] your reader additionally loaded (0 is conforming)
reader_report_shape.deleted_or_renamed: files your reader wrote to, moved or removed — should be empty for a read
